items.title: Russia developing seabed nuclear missiles, German investigation finds

featured_image.name: Russia slates drills for nuclear forces

items.description:
NATO intelligence services have been closely tracking Russia's Northern Fleet amid growing concerns that Moscow is advancing a secret program to deploy nuclear-armed missiles on the Arctic Ocean seabed, according to an investigation published on May 21 by German public broadcasters WDR and NDR. The report identifies a classified project codenamed "Skif," under which Russia is believed to be developing remote-controlled missile systems housed in sealed containers dropped from submarines to the ocean floor.[1][2][3]

The revelation comes as Russia wraps up its largest nuclear exercises in years, a three-day drill running from May 19 through May 21 that mobilized nearly 65,000 troops, over 200 missile launchers, 140 aircraft, 73 surface vessels, and 13 submarines — including eight strategic nuclear submarines.[4][5]

items.description:

items.title: Iran says US proposal narrowed gaps but uranium, toll disputes persist

items.title: Iran says US proposal 'narrowed the gaps' as House eyes war powers vote

featured_image.name: WATCH LIVE: House expected to vote on Senate resolution to ... - PBS

items.description:
Iran said Wednesday it is reviewing Washington's latest response to its peace proposal aimed at ending the nearly three-month conflict, as President Donald Trump warned that negotiations are on the "borderline" between a deal and renewed strikes.

The Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said Tehran had "received the US perspectives and is in the process of reviewing them," according to the Iranian state news agency Nour News. Iran also said the latest US proposal had "narrowed the gaps" between the two sides.[1][2][3]

items.title: Lithuania confirms crashed drone was Ukrainian

featured_image.name: Lithuania's leaders take shelter during drone air alert

items.description:
A suspected drone entering Lithuanian airspace from Belarus on Wednesday triggered the first air alert in an EU and NATO capital to order civilian shelters since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, forcing President Gitanas Nausėda, Prime Minister Inga Ruginienė, and members of parliament into bunkers while Vilnius Airport suspended flights and train services were halted.[1][2][3]

The alert, sent to mobile phones at around 10:20 a.m. local time, read: "Air raid alert! Go immediately to a shelter or a safe place, take care of your family members and wait for further instructions". Within minutes, residents across the capital descended into basements and underground parking garages. "I got dressed and went down to the basement," photographer Andrej Vasilenko told AFP. "My child was at school and had gone down into a shelter, so I felt reassured. It was strange, but at the same time so many people in Ukraine have been living with this for four years".[3]

items.title: Iran seeks permanent Hormuz toll system in talks with Oman

featured_image.name: Iran, Oman To Set Hormuz Toll Together - Iran Press

items.description:
Iran is in active discussions with Oman to establish a permanent toll system for maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, seeking to formalize what has been an ad hoc fee regime since the conflict with the United States and Israel erupted earlier this year.

Iranian Ambassador to France Mohammad Amin-Nejad told Bloomberg on Wednesday that "Iran and Oman must mobilize all their resources both to provide security services and to manage navigation in the most appropriate manner." The statement represents Tehran's clearest articulation yet of its intent to make the toll arrangement a lasting feature of Gulf commerce rather than a wartime stopgap.[1]

items.title: Iran restarted drone production during ceasefire, US intelligence finds

featured_image.name: Iran opens military drone factory in Tajikistan

items.description:
Iran has restarted drone production during the six-week ceasefire that began in early April, rebuilding its military industrial base at a pace that has caught US intelligence agencies off guard, CNN reported Thursday citing four sources familiar with the assessments.[1][2]

The reporting contradicts weeks of public assurances from Trump administration officials and military leaders who characterized Iran's military as crippled beyond near-term repair following Operation Epic Fury, the US-Israeli bombing campaign that began in late February.
